newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European consumers call for soy labelling.
newsitem.headline: European consumers call for soy labelling.

text.p: European Consumers' Organisation BEUC joined calls on Wednesday for mandatory labelling of U.S. gene-modified soybeans and their derived products.

The group said European consumers should be told if gene-modified strains from the current U.S. harvest are used in the array of foods containing soy protein or oil, including confectionery, cakes, soups, sauces, baby food and many others.
"BEUC demands that these products be labelled so that consumers can exercise their right to choose whether to eat them or not," it said in a statement.

The Brussels-based BEUC (European Consumers' Organisation) called on exporters and food manufacturers to separate genetically modified beans, developed by Monsanto Co. of the U.S., from ordinary ones to allow identification.
It also urged EU governments and the European Parliament, which are currently discussing new EU rules for gene-modified foods, to include labelling in their list of requirements.
The call follows similar ones from environmental groups and from EuroCommerce, which represents the retail and wholesale sector in 20 European countries.
This year's U.S. harvest, due for export to Europe in the coming weeks, includes the first batches of the modified soybeans, which Monsanto developed to be resistant to its "Roundup" herbicide.
Monsanto says its product is safe and has been declared as such by authorities in the U.S., Europe and Japan.
But the environmental group Greenpeace says dangers of allergic reactions cannot be ruled out and the impact on the environment is unknown.
Europe is heavily dependent on soybeans, which make up more than half of all oilseeds processed here.
The U.S. supplies 60 percent of the total.
